title: Sampling-horizon cohortization for quantization calibration dataset packs
creator: Marco Li
description: Design and implement a sampling strategy that produces per-domain calibration dataset packs from live production prompts. Packs must support FP8 and INT8 calibration workflows, preserve tenant privacy, and create small, representative bundles that bound quantization accuracy regressions across domain slices.
background: We need compact, reproducible calibration bundles derived from production traffic for quant profile tuning (FP8/INT8). Existing approaches either over-index on global frequency (losing tail behavior) or on heavy stratification (producing large packs). Prior tickets explored stratified reservoir sampling and domain fingerprints; this ticket experiments with a time-aware 'sampling horizon' that cohortizes prompts into horizon windows and then uses multi-criteria scoring to choose exemplars per domain.
proposed_solution: 1) Define domain extractors and domain granularity (product area, intent tag, and tenant). 2) Partition recent production traffic into contiguous time horizons (e.g., 24h, 7d, 30d). 3) For each domain x horizon, compute per-prompt signals: token-length, response-length, rare-token-score (TF-IDF across corpora), latency-tier, and model-failure-flag. 4) Score prompts with a weighted function that emphasizes recency and tail cases, with an explicit cap per-tenant to preserve budget. 5) Apply exemplar anchoring: include top-N exemplars per domain and additional diversity samples via k-means on embedding space (mini-cluster seeds). 6) Produce final pack with deterministic ordering and metadata (seed, horizon, sampling-seed) and create holdout validation split. 7) Wire pack generation into the calibration pipeline and run FP8/INT8 quantization validation harness to measure accuracy deltas against baseline. Tunable knobs: horizon weights, rare-token multiplier, tenant caps, exemplar N. Implementation notes: pipeline runs as batch job in infra/etl, outputs compressed packs to s3://redwood-quant-calibration/packs/{domain}/{yyyyMMdd}/.

acceptance_criteria: Per-domain packs generated deterministically and stored in s3 with metadata
Holdout validation split exists and is reproducible
FP8 and INT8 validation runs for each pack produce accuracy regressions <= 1.5% absolute vs baseline for high-volume domains and bounded degradation for long-tail domains
Tenant-level sample caps enforced (no pack contains > 2% prompts from any single tenant unless explicitly allowed)
End-to-end pipeline has monitoring: pack size, token-distribution summary, and generation latency
Security review signed off for PII scrubbing and pack retention policy
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting — agreed on horizon windows 24h/7d/30d and initial domain granularity (product-area + intent). Action: Marco to publish taxonomy.

2025-02-19: Prototype horizon windowing implemented; small driver created to extract signals and compute rare-token-score. Early tests show rare-token multiplier increases token-entropy by ~12% in sample packs.
2025-02-24: Security reviewed PII scrubber approach (hash + canonicalize URLs); Security requested additional tenant opt-out mechanism. Blocker: legal needs retention policy clarified.

2025-03-01: Generated first set of packs for 10 domains and ran INT8 calibration on a 7B model; average top-1 token accuracy delta: 1.2% for high-volume domains, 2.8% for some tail domains. Preparing follow-up tuning on scoring weights.

2025-03-04: Benchmarks team submitted PR with harness and baseline scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/492. Next step: tune exemplar N and mini-cluster radius to reduce tail degradation.
decisions: Use deterministic random seed per-pack to make sampling reproducible (decision recorded 2025-02-14)
Horizon windows selected: 24h/7d/30d to balance recency and stability (2025-02-14)
Tenant cap set to 2% default; exceptions require PM sign-off (2025-02-24)
Holdout split will be 10% stratified by domain and horizon for validation runs (2025-02-28)
blockers: Legal signoff on retention policy for per-tenant pack storage (open)
Need access to the canonical embedding index for mini-clustering (infra quota currently limited)
Edge-case: very small domains (<200 prompts/week) produce unstable cluster centroids — fallback to reservoir sampling needed
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers should validate that exemplar anchoring does not overfit to a single tenant and that mini-cluster seeds preserve semantic diversity. Pay special attention to the rare-token multiplier effect on token distribution and downstream cost during calibration runs.
validation_plan: 1) For each generated pack run FP8 and INT8 quantization with the standard harness. 2) Compute token-level accuracy, log-prob deltas, and end-user metric proxies (e.g., intent-match score). 3) Compare against baseline runs from pre-quantized float32 model. 4) If tail degradation > 3% absolute, iterate on scoring weights and increase diversity quota for that domain. 5) Store calibration reports alongside packs for audits.
